719: (13) It is permitted to place a jug of water or other liquids in a kli sheni that has warm water in it; but in a kli rishon it is forbidden.
722: (19) 'In a kli sheni that has water' — in the Gemara in chapter Kira it states that R' told R' Shimon bar Avdimi: take it in a kli sheni and place it. And we wrote in Yoreh De'ah at the end of siman 92 that if one draws with an empty vessel from the kli rishon, that vessel has the status of a kli rishon.
724: (33) 'In a kli sheni' — and see Yoreh De'ah, I wrote in the name of the Taz that if one draws in an empty vessel from the kli rishon, that vessel has the status of a kli rishon and it is forbidden to place a jug in it.
732: (86) 'A jug of water' — even water alone without a vessel it is also permitted to mix in a kli sheni as stated in seif 12. The jug is specified because of the end of the clause, to teach us that in a kli rishon it is forbidden.
734: (87) 'In a kli sheni' — it is called a kli sheni when the hot water was poured from the kli rishon in which it was boiled into this vessel. It is permitted even when yad soledes bo. But if one draws in an empty vessel directly from the kli rishon, that vessel has the status of a kli rishon.
736: (81) 'That has hot water in it' — this seif deals with a vessel filled with water, and asks whether it is permitted to place it inside hot water in order to warm the water within it.
738: (82) 'Forbidden' — because the kli rishon also cooks the water in the jug.
741: 'But in a kli rishon it is forbidden' — it appears that if the cold water in the upper vessel is so great that it could not possibly be cooked, it is permitted, for it is no worse than the case where a vessel intervenes.
743: A food that comes as a solid piece, such as a piece of meat: some are stringent and hold that it retains heat inside, and even in a kli sheni it should be regarded as a kli rishon as long as the hand is scalded in it. And one should be stringent in this.
745: The poskim disagree about how to view the broth inside a ladle — whether as a kli rishon or kli sheni. And it appears as halacha that it is a kli sheni, but if it remained in the ladle for a lengthy time it may be treated as a kli rishon.
